correctness.rationale: The nilpotency criterion is equivalent to absence of fixed points for increasing partial injections. The source characterization partitions all successive gap pairs into (1,1), even/even at least 2, or odd/odd at least 3; removal of a final graph pair bijectively gives the polynomial recurrence. For ranks n-k, omitted-coordinate sequences in [0,k] force any nonconstant displacement to use at least five omissions. Shift-restriction counts yield the claimed coefficients, and explicit n>=7 examples attain defect five. Direct independent fence-order enumeration matches every rank coefficient for n<=9, with further exact and boundary checks through n=20.

value.rationale: Nilpotency and rank are intrinsic transformation-semigroup invariants. The theorem computes all rank strata by an exact finite recurrence on an infinite natural monoid family and identifies a sharp defect boundary where all high-rank nilpotents are translations but the first nonuniform graph appears at defect five. This separates the geometry of fence/parity injections from unrestricted order-preserving injections and is not just an unmotivated numeric table or textbook special case.
